function: OTFS channel estimation (encoder-decoder denoiser) and symbol detection (MLP denoiser) in the delay-Doppler domain, inside a plug-and-play framework (pp. 1-2, 7-9).
system: Single-antenna OTFS link, no RIS; N=20 slots, M=20 subcarriers, 3 GHz, 7.5 kHz spacing, 4QAM, rectangular pulses (pp. 5, 9, 10, 13).
method: Plug-and-play ADMM with learned denoisers: residual encoder-decoder CNN (estimation) and 3-hidden-layer MLP (detection); offline MSE training on noisy-clean pairs, called unsupervised in the abstract (pp. 1, 7-9).
data_channel: Self-generated Monte-Carlo delay-Doppler channels, P=5 paths, random indices, kmax=3, lmax=4; 90,000 training and 10,000 validation samples; 2,000 test realizations; no standard model (p. 10).
test_conditions: Denoisers trained with Gaussian noise 0-50 dB; training channel conditions not stated. Tested over SNR with integer, fractional Doppler, fractional delay and Doppler, P=3-5, and CSI error (pp. 10-12).
baselines: Estimation: LS, LMMSE, HQS, EM-SBL, ADMM (classical) and CDRN (learned). Detection: LS, LMMSE, MPA, OAMP (all classical); no learned detector compared (pp. 10-12).
metrics: NMSE for channel estimation; BER for detection and for sequential estimation plus detection; BER versus CSI error; running time; convergence over iterations (pp. 9-12).
complexity: Table I (p. 9): PnP-SD online O(M^3 N + I_L sum z_{l-1} z_l), 0.0028 s; offline training 518.2742 s; LS and LMMSE O(M^3 N^3); no PnP-CE entry.
q1_support: p. 10: "we generate the dataset using the Monte-Carlo method"; p. 10: "the associated delay and Doppler indices for each channel path are randomly selected"; a custom delay-Doppler channel, with no standardized or measured model.
q2_support: p. 2: "maintains robustness across diverse channel conditions without requiring retraining"; p. 11: "we evaluate the robustness of the algorithm under different dispersive OTFS channel conditions"; the paper never states which conditions the training set covers.
q3_support: p. 10: "the LS method, the LMMSE method"; p. 10: "the convolutional deep residual network (CDRN) [13]"; p. 10: "error (NMSE) across various SNR levels, is illustrated in"
q4_support: p. 9: "Table I: Computational Complexities and Running Times of Different Algorithms"; p. 9: "the proposed detector exhibits significantly lower computational complexity"
q5_support: p. 10: "we generate the dataset using the Monte-Carlo method"; the paper gives no code or data link and uses no public dataset.
notes: PDF is the arXiv version 2503.11102v2 (17 Nov 2025). Page 1 shows no DOI, so the match with 10.1109/tcomm.2025.3636093 rests on title and content only; nothing contradicts it. Area 4 wins over 1 and 2 because estimation and detection are done in the delay-Doppler domain. The link is single-antenna (p. 13: 'This work has focused on the single-antenna case'), which OTFS works admit. q2 is borderline: p. 2 claims robustness across channel conditions without retraining, and Figs. 8-9 (p. 11) test fractional Doppler and P=3, 4, but the paper never says what the training set contains, so it is 0. q3 rests on estimation only (CDRN is the learned baseline); all detection baselines are classical. q4 rests on PnP-SD only; Table I has no PnP-CE row. q1 and q5 are 0: the channel is self-generated and nothing is released.
